findings.title: realpath failure drops alias root starts
findings.body: In _guard_starts the loop does os.path.normpath, then os.path.realpath, then _alias_forms inside one try that swallows OSError and ValueError. A raise from realpath skips alias starts for that base and every later base. _alias_limit_exceeded only runs _walk_alias_forms, so a realpath failure is not by itself a hard block. CPython's default realpath (strict=False) usually absorbs link errors internally, and no openable allow was shown from this diff alone. .claude/hooks/dcp_surface_guard.py _guard_starts; _alias_limit_exceeded OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Exported file_repo_root helper returns only the nearest .git above realpath
findings.body: [.claude/hooks/dcp_surface_guard.py] file_repo_root(file_path, fallback) (lines 230-261) resolves os.path.realpath first and stops at the first ancestor directory containing a .git file or directory. While surface_guard_block and surface_guard_warnings no longer call file_repo_root (they use _guard_roots, which checks project_root plus all enclosing .git directories across lexical, realpath, and alias starts), file_repo_root remains exported for Wave 2B W09 per T01. Any downstream caller that relies on file_repo_root alone for security blocking would remain susceptible to a planted inner .git file or a symlinked directory resolving outside the repository. Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Direct edit to an external directory target of a checkout's red-lane symlink is not detectable by forward/upward path walking
findings.body: [.claude/hooks/dcp_surface_guard.py] If a checkout's red-lane directory (e.g., services/task-orchestrator) is a symlink pointing to an external directory outside all git checkouts, and an edit addresses a file directly via that external path without traversing any checkout or any symlink leading through a checkout, neither _guard_roots nor _walk_alias_forms can associate the external path with the checkout's red lane. Amendment 10 removed the block message suggestion to use the real path, and AMENDMENT_10.md / AMENDMENT_11.md / G02_RETURN.md document this pre-existing limitation for follow-up design. Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Symlink hop counter tracks recursion depth rather than sequential hop count, and dual-key warnings report one surface per call
findings.body: [.claude/hooks/dcp_surface_guard.py] (1) In _walk_alias_forms (lines 78-100), hops is incremented only on recursive symlink target walks (hops + 1) rather than cumulative sequential symlink resolutions across a path; however, sequential non-reverting symlinks double the form count at each link and trip _MAX_ALIAS_FORMS (64) at ~6 links, while OS kernels reject >32 total symlink resolutions with ELOOP on open. (2) In surface_guard_warnings (lines 563-578), when a single tool call supplies both file_path and notebook_path pointing to two distinct unwarned contract surfaces, the loop breaks after caching and returning the warning for the first unwarned surface only. Corroborating auditor. OPERATOR: decision pending.
